A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have demonstrated the presence of a PAP-I in bovine whole-brain, which is capable of cleaving a wide range of pGlu-containing neuropeptides and which displays a high degree of homology with the PAP-I activity observed in other mammalian systems.
the bovine brain PAP-I enzyme is a monomeric enzyme with broad pyroglutarimyl substrate specificity.
the soluble bovine whole brain PAP-I has been successfully purified and characterised, and that the results obtained compare well with those reported for this enzyme in other mammalian species.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we have identified a novel, soluble PAP activity in bovine brain that is capable of cleaving the N-terminal pGlu residue from a wide variety of neuropeptides and which may play an important role in the inactivation of neuropeptide hormones in brain.

we have purified and characterised a novel PAP activity in bovine whole-brain cytosol, which displays a broad pyroglutaric substrate specificity and which is inhibited by a variety of agents, including 2-pyrroline, a pGlu analogue.

the bovine brain PAP-I is capable of removing the pGlu residue from a wide range of pGlu-containing peptides, including TRH, LTH, NPY, neurotensins, bombesin and the pGlu-containing fragment of amyloid beta (A-beta 1-28).
